thread.title: Apple had the best quarter ever for any wearable vendor in 2017 (AAPL)

author: BusinessInsider
title: Apple had the best quarter ever for any wearable vendor in 2017 (AAPL)
text:
Apple had the best quarter ever for any wearable vendor in 2017 (AAPL) Posted By: BusinessInsider February 8, 2018 
This story was delivered to BI Intelligence Apps and Platforms Briefing subscribers hours before appearing on Business Insider. To be the first to know, please click here . 
Apple shipped 8 million Apple Watches in Q4 2017, marking the best quarter ever not just for Apple, but for any wearable vendor, according to a new report from Canalys. 
Apple’s newest additions to the lineup, the Series 3 and the Series 3 with LTE connectivity, played an outsize role in this growth. T 
he new line was only released in September, but accounted for nearly half of total shipments for 2017, meaning it sold 8.8 million units in just the final four months of the year; subsequently, the vast majority of the 8 million Apple Watches shipped in the three months of Q4. 
The Apple Watch’s stand-out Q4 helped accelerate full-year growth after a slowdown in 2016. The 18.3 million Apple Watches sold in 2017 represented growth of 54% from the 11.9 million it shipped in 2016, which was down 1% from 12 million in 2015. 
Notably, the stats indicate that stand-alone connectivity — and the added features and use cases that come with it — is a draw for smartwatches, but not yet a must-have. 
The Series 3 Apple Watch with added cellular functionality accounted for 2.4 million shipments in 2017, while the noncellular version accounted for more than double, with 6.4 million shipments. While the Series 3 with cellular connectivity has yet to generate more demand than its unconnected version, with the new LTE-version in the hands of consumers it’s likely new use cases for the stand-alone Apple Watch will emerge, effectively driving adoption of the Series 3 with LTE throughout 2018.
